To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a promoter mutation associated with the hptoglobin 2- 1 modified phenotype decreases promoter function and responsiveness to interleu-kin-6.

an A to C substitution in the promoter region at position -61 of the haptoglobin gene decreases transcriptional activity in hepatoma cells and that this mutation renders the haptoglobin promoter unresponsive to induction by interleukin 6.
a single base substitution (A to C) at -61 in the Hp2 gene promoter decreases transcriptional activity in HepG2 cells and abolishes the response to interleukin 6 in Hep3B2 hepatoma cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the molecular mechanisms underlying the haptoglobin phenotype.
the identification and characterization of the genetic determinants of the human hapticin 2-1 mod phenotype and their functional significance in the context of the haptoglobin gene.
the identification of genetic markers for the Hp2- 1mod phenotype and the characterization of the molecular basis of the Hp2- lmod phenotype.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Hp2 allele is not expressed at all in individuals who are Hp2-1 mod.
the Hp2 allele is less active than the Hp1 allele and that the -61C substitution is a major factor in this difference.
the -61C substitution, which is the major mutation associated with the Hp 2-1 mod phenotype, causes a reduction in transcriptional activity of the Hp2 promoter in HepG2 cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Hp2 allele, with the -61A base substitution, is more transcriptionally active in HepG2 cells than the Hp2 allele with the -61 C substitution and that both alleles are equally transcriptionally active in the Hep3B2 cell line, which does not normally express haptoglobin.

the Hp2 allele is expressed at a lower level than the Hp1 allele because of an A-to-C base change in the Hp2 promoter at nucleotide position-61, and the Hp2 allele has a reduced response to interleukin 6 because of a T-to-A base change at nucleotide position –104 in the Hp2 allele.
the Hp2 allele has a lower transcriptional efficiency and is less responsive to interleukin 6 than the Hp1 allele.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can use the CAT reporter system to investigate the function of the Hp gene promoter in the context of the human genome.
the A to C base substitution in the Hp2 promoter is associated with decreased transcriptional activity and interleukin- 6 responsiveness.
we have demonstrated the importance of the -61C substitution in the promoter of the Hp2-allele in the regulation of Hp gene expression.
